title: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition

topics.title: Perfect competition: defining features and price-taking

concepts.learning_objective: State the four defining features of a perfectly competitive market and why each matters.
Explain why firms and buyers in a perfectly competitive market behave as price-takers.

topics.title: Revenue: total, average and marginal revenue

concepts.learning_objective: Compute TR, AR and MR for a price-taking firm and show that MR = AR = p.
Interpret the TR curve and the price line as the perfectly elastic demand curve facing a firm.
Explain why profit is maximised where price equals marginal cost.
Explain why marginal cost must be non-decreasing at the profit-maximising output.
Apply the conditions p >= AVC in the short run and p >= AC in the long run to the decision to produce.

topics.title: Short run and long run supply curve of a firm

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the short run supply curve of a firm from its SMC and AVC curves.
Derive the long run supply curve of a firm from its LRMC and LRAC curves.

topics.title: Shut down point, normal profit and break-even point

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the short run and long run shut down points of a firm.
Distinguish normal profit, super-normal profit and the break-even point.
Calculate the opportunity cost of an activity as the gain foregone from the next best alternative.

topics.title: Determinants of a firm's supply curve

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how technological progress shifts a firm's supply curve.
Explain how a change in input prices shifts a firm's supply curve.
Analyse how a unit tax changes a firm's cost curves and long run supply curve.
Derive the market supply curve by horizontally summing the supply curves of individual firms.
Explain how a change in the number of firms shifts the market supply curve.
Define and calculate the price elasticity of supply by the percentage method.
Use the geometric method to judge the elasticity of straight line supply curves.
